xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4638: Run gauntlet lanes on any linked machine: desktop, laptop and Fly VMs

plan.title: Run gauntlet lanes on any linked machine: desktop, laptop and Fly VMs
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: One lane-door protocol split across two machines: the owner door, the home stand-in, the follower that mirrors reports, the views, and wait/stop/reap must all exist for a single remote lane to report back to its orchestrator, so no subset ships useful behavior on its own. The issue is already one decomposed work item (W-WORK3) of epic PAN-2350; the new-VM half (--machine fly, remote.auto_fly, gauntlet.fly.max_vms) is deferred to PAN-4743. Most of the file count is the per-item test files and the six documentation pages the PRD requires.

narratives.Problem: pan lane start --machine resolves a target but refuses any machine other than this one ('Lanes on other machines arrive with PAN-4638'). A gauntlet loop therefore saturates the orchestrator's machine with heavy critics even when the laptop or a linked Fly machine is idle, and the CPU-pressure refusal can only make the loop wait.
narratives.Proposal: Split the lane door: home keeps every run rule (parent, launcher standing, run, critic link and default --at, iteration, idempotency, model/harness) and calls a new owner work door POST /api/machines/work/lanes that only creates the worktree, brief, parentless lane row stamped with home's environment, and the runtime. Home records the lane in an on-disk stand-in (~/.overdeck/remote-lanes/<name>/, never a conversations row), a follower mirrors the owner's reports and state into it, and lane views, wait, stop and reap read or forward through it. The merged conversation list stamps lane facts on the owner's linked row so the dashboard nests remote lanes under the orchestrator. Details: .pan/drafts/PAN-4638.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- --machine fly that provisions a new Fly VM per lane, remote.auto_fly and gauntlet.fly.max_vms (owned by PAN-4743); --machine fly keeps answering 400 fly-unavailable
- Fixing the Fly machine bugs #4738, #4739, #4740, #4741
- Orchestrator lanes on another machine (refused with 400)
- Forwarding pan tell conv-<name> from home to a remote lane (use pan tell @<label>/<name>)
- Stopping remote lanes when the orchestrator conversation ends
- A machine column on the gauntlet progress page (assets/gauntlet-index.html)
- Harnesses other than Claude Code on Fly machines (#4296)
- Inserting any conversations row on home for a remote lane
- Inventing a numeric id for a remote lane
- Changing the D-19 placement rule in src/lib/anywhere/placement.ts

autoDecisions.summary: Defer --machine fly (new VM), remote.auto_fly and gauntlet.fly.max_vms to PAN-4743
autoDecisions.rationale: PAN-4743 already owns --machine fly across start/worker/conversations; the W-WORK3 done-when (critics on a Fly VM) is met by a Fly machine created with pan machines add-fly and chosen by label or Auto, and keeping the new-VM path out keeps this issue inside the finalize size limits.

autoDecisions.summary: A linked Fly machine is an ordinary Auto candidate
autoDecisions.rationale: It is linked and already paid for; the D-19 Fly exclusion governs creating a new VM, which PAN-4743 owns. placement.ts is unchanged.

autoDecisions.summary: Remote lanes are on-disk stand-ins, never conversations rows
autoDecisions.rationale: Epic D-5 keeps other machines' conversations out of conversations because rows there drive liveness, costs, lanes and the PR sweep; PAN-4651's worker stand-ins set the same precedent.

autoDecisions.summary: Home allocates the lane's conversation name and the owner refuses an existing name
autoDecisions.rationale: The same name on both machines lets conv-<name> key the report store on both, so every existing report reader works on mirrored reports; createConversation would otherwise vacate a same-name row.

autoDecisions.summary: Pairing and LaneView key on lane names; remote lanes have id null
autoDecisions.rationale: Remote lanes have no local rowid and FKs cannot reference stand-ins; names are unique across home and its stand-ins.

autoDecisions.summary: A local critic of a remote builder records the link in agents/conv-<critic>/lane-link.json
autoDecisions.rationale: critic_of_conversation_id is an FK to local rows; a write-once sidecar next to the brief keeps the launch fact without a schema change.

autoDecisions.summary: --reuse follows the newest lane's machine; --machine with --reuse is 400; orchestrator lanes stay home
autoDecisions.rationale: A reuse must happen in the existing directory, which lives on one machine; an orchestrator lane elsewhere would list its lanes only there.

autoDecisions.summary: Remote launches skip home's CPU check and the owner runs its own
autoDecisions.rationale: The point of placing the lane elsewhere is to avoid home's CPU pressure; the owner is the machine that takes the load.

autoDecisions.summary: The follower does not stop remote lanes when the orchestrator ends
autoDecisions.rationale: Local lanes do not cascade-stop either; matching behavior avoids surprising data loss.
